name: Discrete Mathematics / Дискретна математика
ai_policy: AI allowed as a trainer for definitions and theory. Not for graded homework, quizzes or tests. Warn: check AI math manually.
assessment: Quizzes: 6 x 6 points, UNANNOUNCED, ~every two weeks, 15 min, true/false per task — each week's lecture must be learned before practice
Graded homework: 2 x 3 points before each midterm; missed deadline = 0
Grading: full reasoning required; correct answer without justification = 25%
Pre-recorded lectures (flipped): watch before the week's practices; problems levels A/B/C
notes: Hard for the student and the largest course (6 credits). Books: Rosen 'Discrete Mathematics and its Applications', Richmond & Richmond, Bickle 'Fundamentals of Graph Theory', Боднарчук & Олійник.

topics.title: Propositional logic: formulas, interpretations, connectives, truth tables
Predicate logic: quantifiers, free and bound variables, equivalences
Naive set theory, set operations, inclusion proofs
Binary relations: diagonal, inverse, composition; the six main properties
Partially ordered sets: Hasse diagrams, cones, maximal and minimal elements
Functional relations, images and preimages, composition
Boolean functions, DNF, CNF, perfect normal forms
Graph basics: handshaking lemma, paths and cycles, trees, bipartite graphs, adjacency matrix
Walks, connectivity, reachability; coloring, chromatic, clique and independence numbers
